en.caption: Random Curses
rows: The previous owner, a vampire, will hunt down the purchasers in {@dice 1d4} weeks
The item requires two attunement slots (if the item does not normally require attunement, it now requires one)
After {@dice 2d4} days, the item disappears, returning to the Shadar-Kai's store
A commoner will find the new owner after {@dice 1d4} weeks and explain the item was stolen from her and that she needs the money from selling it or else her family will starve

The item is part of a game between two rakshasa. They gamble to see how long each owner of the item survives after obtaining it. Within {@dice 3d6} days one of the rakshasa will attempt to kill the owner
Within {@dice 1d6} weeks an adult gold dragon will confront the new owner when she recognizes the item as belonging to the lair of her recently slain child
1 week after first obtaining the item, the new owner loses {@dice 4d4} from their hit point maximum until a {@spell greater restoration} spell is cast upon the item
Within {@dice 1d6} days of purchasing the item, it becomes a normal version of its base item
Each day the item changes to a random color
The item begins to stink after {@dice 1d4} weeks, giving disadvantage to anyone within 10 ft. making Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) checks involving smell.
en.name: Random Curses

en.caption: Dankwood Adventure Hooks
rows: A flute, that when played, summons a {@creature pegasus}. (Where does the {@creature pegasus} fly to if you get on its back?)
A carved wooden bird that comes to life when picked up and leads the adventurers to the entrance of a cave. (What treasures are in the cave?)
A {@creature pixie} flies up to you and asks if you would help to chase a {@creature troll} away from its village. (How do you get rid of a dangerous troll?)
A hunter is in the forest looking for a rare elk with golden antlers. (Either help the hunter catch the elk or help the elk escape the hunter.)

An elf who claims to be of royal blood is seeking refuge in the Dankwood. He is being hunted by rival elves and is willing to pay gold for your help. (Is the elf really who he says he is? Who are the rival elves?)
A gnome rushes up to you, hands you a golden key, and tells you, "Find the crystal cave and save me." before turning to stone!
One of your nets traps a {@creature tiger}. As you are figuring out what to do with it, the {@creature tiger} speaks and claims that it was once a halfling that was cursed by an evil wizard.
A bounty hunter is on the lookout for a criminal. Is the criminal actually bad or is the bounty hunter bad?
en.name: Dankwood Adventure Hooks

en.caption: Island Environments
rows: Frozen. The island is magically frozen or is a floating iceberg. Perhaps something lies locked within.
Sargassum. The island is a dense layer of seaweed that has developed its own ecosystem of strange beasts and trapped sailors.
Living. The island is actually a gigantic slumbering creature—potentially unbeknown to its residents.
Mirage. Magical phenomena surround a mundane island with tempting or treacherous illusions.
Nyx Shard. The island is a manifestation of Nyx, a recreation of a land from the distant past or completely from fiction.
Idyllic. The island has beautiful weather and abundant fruit—so much so that some might consider never leaving.
Lost Ruin. The island is all that survived a calamity that destroyed a legendary city.
Gateway. The island is inherently magical, perhaps being an intrusion from a bizarre demiplane or the dream of a sleeping demigod.
Promised Land. The island is a gift from a god to a favored individual or population, specially tailored to suit their whims.
Divine Refuge. A god created this island to be a personal getaway, making it a reflection of the world as it would appear if they were in complete control.

A group of {@creature Thug||thugs} vandalizes market stalls whose owners don't pay a weekly protection fee.
{@creature Cultist||Cultists} of Pharika plot to spike the wine at a party in the agora with an experimental poison.
A snake charmer overreaches when he unsuccessfully attempts to control an {@creature amphisbaena|GoS} (see {@area chapter 6|00e|x}) during a performance.
A disgraced priest of Ephara releases a horde of anvilwrought creatures (see {@area chapter 6|028|x}) on a crowd gathered at the agora.
A {@creature mage} politician uses enchantment magic to spread rumors about rivals.

en.caption: Coastal Temple Villains
rows: A {@creature kraken} threatens to destroy the temple if worshipers don't pay tribute to the creature.
A {@creature Naiad|MOT} hides inside the temple and murders fishers who worship here for their crimes against the sea.
A group of sirens (see the {@creature Harpy||harpies} entry in {@area chapter 6|031|x}) take over the temple and lure new victims inside to drown themselves during high tide.
A {@creature priest} of Thassa falsely convinces elderly worshipers that giving more wealth to the temple increases the length of time they live.
A {@creature giant octopus} under the effects of the {@spell awaken} spell hunts in the temple at high tide.
A rageful {@creature triton master of waves|MOT} believes everyone in a temple is secretly serving a kraken and begins murdering them.
en.name: Coastal Temple Villains

en.caption: Underworld Adventures
rows: In Phylias, find and bargain for information with your least favorite dead acquaintance or family member.
Smuggle the puppy of an {@creature Underworld cerberus|MOT} into the mortal world.
Find and free a lost hero from the Labyrinth of Memories on Nerono.
Free a legendary lost ship and the souls aboard from the endless Nerono whirlpool they're trapped within.
Meet with your family's most legendary member in Ilysia and prove yourself worthy of their name.
Steal a legendary, long-shattered treasure from its resting place in Ilysia's Citadel of Destiny.
Seek out a long-dead foe and learn how they're keeping you from being magically resurrected.
Discover a secret from an infamous member of your family who became a {@creature typhon|MOT} (see {@area chapter 6|041|x}).
Save a god's favored worshiper from a cruel punishment in the Underworld—even though they've been dead for hundreds of years.
Sever one of the massive chains of Tizerus, releasing the ancient being it binds.
Lead an immortal anvilwrought to Erebos's palace and convince the god to let the construct die.
Discover why Erebos is no longer allowing certain individuals to die.
Coerce a {@creature night hag} into granting a morbid prophecy by stealing its eye.
Learn a secret way to escape the Underworld from one of the titans.
Find the lost secret of a long-dead warlord that now rests with the villain's misera.
Discover from a {@creature woe strider|MOT} (see {@area chapter 6|042|x}) how to escape the bonds of destiny.
Defeat a host of legendary villains in Agonas's Stadium of Dishonor.
Prevent one of your ancestors from transforming into an {@creature eater of hope|MOT}.
Travel to Erebos's palace and recover a secret from one who failed to bargain for their release.
Seek out Klothys's domain and learn from her oracles how you're destined to escape the Underworld.
en.name: Underworld Adventures

en.caption: Iroas's Divine Schemes
rows: Iroas inspires a brave Akroan general to travel forth with a handpicked army and confront the forces of a powerful and supposedly vulnerable minotaur warlord. The general loses despite Iroas's favor, and Akros is left exposed and poorly defended before a wave of Mogis-worshiping minotaurs.

Heliod, weary of the constant strife between Iroas and Mogis, swears an oath to destroy Mogis with a godly coalition behind him. Erebos, disgusted with Heliod's hubris, forms a group in support of Mogis. Iroas, rather than accepting Heliod's aid, launches a grand campaign of his own against his brother.

Mogis arms one of his champions with an axe capable of sundering the souls of mortal creatures. Iroas wants his champions to procure the weapon so he can lock it away in his armory and thwart his brother. Agents of Erebos also seek to recover the weapon on their master's behalf.
Iroas achieves the victory he has always pursued: he kills his brother, and the world falls into chaos.
en.name: Iroas's Divine Schemes

en.caption: Nylea's Divine Schemes
rows: When the polis of Meletis expands, clearing new land for houses and crops, Nylea decides to punish the polis and destroy it if necessary. Animated trees topple the walls, and Nyxborn beasts invade the city.
Nylea refuses to turn winter into spring unless Karametra agrees to abolish agriculture and yield all cropland back to the forest.

When tensions between Akros and Setessa peak, Nylea blames Iroas for stirring up the conflict and puts Setessa under her protection, expanding the borders of the Nessian Wood to encompass all of Setessa, creating a near-impenetrable fortress filled with dangerous creatures.

Nylea abruptly vanishes. Explorers deep in the Nessian Wood discover her sacred grove abandoned, and the giant chrysalis at its heart empty. What was in the chrysalis? Could it have harmed Nylea? Or did she leave with the creature—and if so, did she do that to protect the creature, or to protect Theros?
en.name: Nylea's Divine Schemes

en.caption: Healing Pools Villains
rows: A group of {@creature Returned Palamnite|MOT|Returned palamnites} invade the pools, believing the waters' magic can restore their lost memories and mortal bodies.
{@creature Naiad|MOT|Naiads} guard the pools, making their own judgments about who is and isn't worthy of the pools' healing magic.
The magic waters of the pools wash out to sea and attract a dying {@creature kraken} to the area.
An {@creature assassin} barters captured humanoid test subjects for poison from the pools' {@creature medusa} priest.
A dying {@creature veteran} who was {@condition poisoned} by the pools slaughters any person who is healed by the waters.
An {@creature oracle|MOT} (see {@area chapter 6|03c|x}) allows the pools' poisons to seep from the caves and contaminate a community.

en.caption: Underworld Crossings Villains
rows: A {@creature Returned palamnite|MOT} seeks to destroy all Underworld crossings so the dead can freely enter the mortal world.
A conquering general captures a number of {@creature Underworld Cerberus|MOT|Underworld cerberi}, plotting to unleash the terrifying beasts during a war.
A greedy {@creature priest} of Erebos steals coins from the dead before they are buried, thereby filling a crossing with stranded souls.

A {@creature nightmare shepherd|MOT} takes over a crossing and doesn't allow souls to pass into the Underworld. As a result, they become {@creature Specter||specters} that harass the living in the mortal world.
A {@creature priest} of Athreos becomes annoyed with the dead returning and sends armies of clergy to secure the mortal side of the crossing.
A {@creature satyr reveler|MOT} seeks to throw an eternal revel! By stealing coins from the dead, the satyr traps souls at his morbid, Tartyx-side bacchanal.

en.caption: Satyr Eccentricities
rows: Flowers are the most amazing things ever. I want to pick them, wear them, and discover their silent secrets.
There isn't a tree or statue that isn't fun to climb.
Nothing wards off bad luck like a jolly dance.
Sometimes talking to a plant really helps.
If stumped, I smoke a pipe. And if I'm going to smoke a pipe, it's going to be a splendid pipe.
I imagine that my clothes are my glorious soul on display for all the world to behold, and I dress accordingly.
Having horns is the best. They are fun to decorate, and they can pop open an amphora, no problem.
If I have something really important to say, I always make sure to sing it.
en.name: Satyr Eccentricities

en.caption: Volcano Temple Villains
rows: An {@creature adult red dragon} tries to make its nest inside the temple, attacking the artisans and priests within.

A {@creature priest} of Mogis infiltrates the volcano and mars its ornate halls, hoping to draw Purphoros's ire and thus cause the volcano to erupt at an unexpected time, killing everyone in the temple.
A obsessed {@creature cult fanatic} is never satisfied with her apprentices' creations and works them to death.
A unit of defeated and desperate {@b hoplites} (see {@area chapter 6|033|x}) raid the temple, steal magical weapons, and prepare to avenge their fallen companions.
An apprentice artisan summons {@creature Fire Elemental||fire elementals} that he can't control to murder his cruel master.
An {@creature iron golem} forged in the temple breaks free of its maker's control and goes on a killing spree.

rows: Hundreds of snakes, spiders, or centipedes crawl from the ground.

A character exhibits a disease's symptoms.

A snakeskin wraps around a way marker or personal possession.
Patterns of clouds or stars slither away, moving with an audible susurrus.

en.caption: Athreos's Quests
rows: Seal a secret path that the Returned use to escape the Underworld.
Strike against one of the necropoleis, either Asphodel or Odunos, curtailing its growth or bringing it to ruin.
Seek out a {@creature lampad|MOT} nymph who has fallen in love with a soul he was supposed to lead to the Underworld.
Hunt down a rampaging cerberus and return it to its place guarding the Underworld.
Reconsecrate a grand but neglected mausoleum, putting the unquiet spirits there to rest.
Defeat an agent of a god who seeks to free a loved one, a mentor, or a champion from the Underworld.

en.caption: Keranos's Divine Schemes
rows: Bored with the temporary beauty of violent weather, Keranos creates a massive, self-perpetuating storm. Over time, the storm grows out of control. Keranos is delighted by his creation.

Dared by Phenax to prove that he can, Keranos inspires eight mortals with eight ingenious ways to destroy the world. As a result, a genius actor, alchemist, inventor, diver, miner, sculptor, thief, and a duplicitous goat all set forth to enact their terrible brilliance.

Keranos finds the spread of mortal knowledge inconsistent and slow. He empowers a champion to grant vast knowledge to any person or beast she touches. The advent of sagacious cattle, wolves, and children greatly disrupts (and unnerves) those who live in the areas through which Keranos's champion travels.

Keranos creates a realm of his own design amid the Dakra Isles, a place where the land and its creatures obey unique physical laws and strange truths. Some of the inhabitants escape the isle and begin infecting the rest of Theros with their alternate reality.
en.name: Keranos's Divine Schemes

en.caption: Athreos's Divine Schemes
rows: Athreos tires of his responsibilities but refuses to abandon them. Secretly, he has allowed the same spirit to be reborn again and again, allowing it to see all of life and death so it might one day take his place. When this apprentice disappears, Athreos refuses to ferry any more souls until his student is returned.

The wealth Athreos collects in payment for his work has gone missing, stolen from his sanctuary at the end of the Tartyx River. The River Guide needs the treasure returned swiftly, not out of greed, but as it is payment for something beyond the gods.

The Rivers That Ring the World are drying up. As the tides recede, great ruins are revealed, rising from the river bottom. Athreos sends agents to the headwaters of the Tartyx River, seeking the cause of the problem before whatever the river had kept drowned emerges.

War between Heliod and Erebos is inevitable. Rather than letting it explode unpredictably, Athreos puts a plan into Motion to mitigate the damage. Ultimately, all it takes to end the war is Heliod's death or Erebos joining the Returned.
en.name: Athreos's Divine Schemes
